beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Care coordination, sanitation, maintenance, compliance, and other difficult work can carry persistent unmet needs.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These markets may demand operational patience rather than an elegant digital demonstration.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book does not assume that an unglamorous industry is automatically profitable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Regulation, procurement, trust, and weak margins can still make execution difficult.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its challenge is to stop using a founder’s social discomfort as a market filter.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The reader is invited to stay close enough to a problem to understand who actually bears it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Psychological distress raises the book’s most uncomfortable commercial question.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Greater recognition and inadequate services can make a real need more visible.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Technology might reduce barriers while also creating new ways to monetize dependence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The difference depends partly on what a company counts as success.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Longer use can mean value in one setting and unresolved vulnerability in another.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book asks whether users can leave more autonomous than they arrived.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That question connects its market analysis to the ethics of product architecture.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Suppose a product worked so well that its customers needed it less often.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Would the business remain viable under its own definition of success?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The ethics chapter places that test inside pricing, design, and operational decisions.
